blocks.text: The **atmosphere** is the gaseous envelope of the Earth, layered by temperature into the **troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere and exosphere**. Its composition (mostly **nitrogen and oxygen**) and the **ozone layer** make life possible.

rows: 0–~12 km; **all weather occurs here**; temp falls with height (**normal lapse rate ~6.5°C/km**).
~12–50 km; contains the **ozone layer** (absorbs UV); ideal for **jet flights**; temp rises.
**Nitrogen ~78%, Oxygen ~21%**, Argon ~0.9%, CO₂ ~0.04%; water vapour & dust variable.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: atmosphere structure & composition

rows: **All weather**; temp falls with height (**normal lapse rate 6.5°C/km**); densest.
**Ozone layer (~15-35 km)** absorbs UV → temp rises; calm → **jet aircraft** fly here.
Ionised; **reflects radio waves**; **auroras**; temp very high.

items: **Composition (by volume)**: **Nitrogen 78%, Oxygen 21%, Argon 0.9%, CO2 0.04%** (rising), plus water vapour, ozone & aerosols (dust).
**Greenhouse gases**: CO2, CH4 (methane), N2O, water vapour, CFCs, O3 — trap outgoing infrared → warming; **ozone (O3) in stratosphere protects; at surface it is a pollutant**.
The **tropopause** separates troposphere & stratosphere; the **ozone hole** (Antarctica) is tackled by the **Montreal Protocol (1987)**.
Troposphere = weather; Stratosphere = ozone; Mesosphere = meteors burn; Ionosphere = radio reflection.
N₂ 78% / O₂ 21%; normal lapse rate 6.5°C/km.

sections.heading: Elements & factors of climate; air masses & fronts

blocks.text: **Weather and climate** are described by **elements** (temperature, pressure, wind, humidity, precipitation) and controlled by **factors** (latitude, altitude, distance from sea, ocean currents, relief, winds). **Air masses** and their boundaries (**fronts**) drive mid-latitude weather.

rows: **Latitude, altitude, continentality, ocean currents, prevailing winds, relief, slope/aspect**.
**Equatorial low, Sub-tropical high, Sub-polar low, Polar high** (4 belts pattern).
**Trade winds, Westerlies, Polar easterlies**; deflected by Coriolis.
**cP, cT, mP, mT**; fronts — **warm, cold, occluded, stationary** (weather boundaries).

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: climate elements, winds, air masses

items: **Factors of climate**: **latitude** (insolation), **altitude** (temp falls), **distance from sea (continentality)**, **ocean currents**, **winds/pressure**, **relief** (windward/leeward, rain-shadow), **ocean currents** & vegetation.
**Pressure belts (7)**: Equatorial Low (doldrums), Sub-tropical Highs (horse latitudes, ~30°), Sub-polar Lows (~60°), Polar Highs.

**Planetary/permanent winds**: **Trade winds** (Highs→Equator, NE & SE), **Westerlies** (Highs→Sub-polar Lows; 'roaring forties'), **Polar Easterlies**; deflected by **Coriolis** (right in N-hemisphere, Ferrel's Law).

**Periodic winds**: **monsoons** (seasonal reversal), land & sea breezes; **local winds** — Loo (India, hot), Chinook (N.America, snow-eater), Foehn (Alps), Mistral (cold, France), Sirocco (hot, Sahara→Europe).
**Air masses** (large uniform air bodies — cP, mT, etc.) meet at **fronts**: **warm, cold, stationary, occluded** — the basis of temperate cyclones/depressions.
**Rainfall types**: **Convectional** (equatorial, afternoon), **Orographic/relief** (windward slopes — heaviest; rain-shadow leeward), **Cyclonic/frontal**.
Distinguish elements (measured) vs factors/controls (latitude, altitude, sea, currents).
Four pressure belts; three planetary winds (trades, westerlies, polar easterlies); fronts = air-mass boundaries.

blocks.text: **Atmospheric disturbances** — cyclones (tropical & temperate), thunderstorms and jet streams — produce much of the world's severe weather, while **climate change** (global warming from greenhouse gases) is altering these patterns — a topic of high current relevance.

rows: Form over warm seas (>26.5°C); **eye, eyewall**; called **cyclones (India), hurricanes (Atlantic), typhoons (Pacific)**; hit AP/Odisha coast.
Mid-latitude, front-based; bring **western disturbances** (NW India winter rain).
Fast upper-air westerlies; **sub-tropical jet** influences the Indian monsoon.
**El Nino** (warm Pacific) → weak monsoon/drought; **La Nina** → good monsoon.
**Greenhouse gases (CO₂, CH₄), global warming, sea-level rise**; Paris Agreement, IPCC.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: cyclones, disturbances & climate change

items: **Tropical cyclones**: form over warm seas (>26.5°C) between 5°–20° lat; called **hurricanes** (Atlantic), **typhoons** (Pacific), **cyclones** (Indian Ocean), **willy-willies** (Australia); a calm **eye** at the centre; India's **IMD names** them (Bay of Bengal > Arabian Sea frequency).
**Temperate (extra-tropical) cyclones**: mid-latitude, front-based, larger & milder; bring winter rain to NW India (**Western Disturbances** from the Mediterranean).
**El Nino–Southern Oscillation (ENSO)**: **El Nino** (warm E-Pacific) → weak Indian monsoon/drought; **La Nina** → good monsoon; **Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD)** positive → good monsoon.

**Climate change**: global warming from GHGs; **IPCC** assessments; **UNFCCC (1992) → Kyoto Protocol (1997) → Paris Agreement (2015, limit to 1.5–2°C, NDCs)**; India's **Panchamrit** & **Net-Zero by 2070** pledge (Glasgow COP26).
Cyclone naming by region; El Nino weakens the Indian monsoon; jet stream steers monsoon onset.
Climate change = GHGs → warming, sea-level rise; IPCC & Paris Agreement.

prelimsPointers: **Tropical cyclones** need warm seas (>26.5°C); have an **eye & eyewall**; **cyclone/hurricane/typhoon** by region.

**Western disturbances** (temperate cyclones from the Mediterranean) bring **winter rain to NW India**.
**Jet streams** — sub-tropical westerly jet influences **monsoon onset & withdrawal**.
**El Nino** (warm eastern Pacific) → **weak monsoon/drought**; **La Nina** → strong monsoon.
**Greenhouse gases** — CO₂, methane (CH₄), N₂O; cause **global warming**.
**IPCC** (assessment reports) & the **Paris Agreement (2015, 1.5-2°C)** address climate change.
Tropical-cyclone names: **hurricane (Atlantic), typhoon (Pacific), cyclone (Indian Ocean), willy-willy (Australia)**.
**Western Disturbances** (Mediterranean origin) → NW India winter rain.
**El Nino → weak monsoon/drought**; **La Nina & positive IOD → good monsoon**.

blocks.text: The **oceans** cover ~71% of Earth and are described by their **relief (physical), salinity/temperature (chemical) and marine life (biological)** characteristics, along with **currents, tides and waves** that regulate global climate.

rows: **Continental shelf → slope → deep-sea plain (abyssal) → trench (deepest — Mariana)**; mid-oceanic ridges.
Avg **~35 ppt**; highest in enclosed seas (Dead Sea, Red Sea); lower near river mouths/poles.
Decreases with depth; **thermocline** separates warm surface from cold deep.
Warm (Gulf Stream, Kuroshio) & cold (Labrador, Humboldt); regulate coastal climate & fisheries.
**Spring tides (new/full moon), Neap tides (quarter moon)**; caused by Moon & Sun gravity.

items: **Relief**: continental **shelf** (richest fishing/oil), **slope**, **deep-sea plain (abyssal)**, **trenches** (deepest — **Mariana/Challenger Deep, ~11 km**), **mid-ocean ridges**, seamounts, guyots.
**Temperature**: falls with depth; the **thermocline** = sharp drop layer; salinity avg **35‰** (highest in enclosed seas — **Dead Sea, Lake Van**; Red Sea ~40‰).

**Currents**: warm (equator→poles, e.g. **Gulf Stream, Kuroshio, N.Atlantic Drift**) & cold (poles→equator, e.g. **Labrador, Benguela, Humboldt/Peru, California**); driven by winds, Coriolis, density; **gyres**; cold+warm meeting → rich fishing (**Grand Banks — Labrador+Gulf Stream**).

**Tides**: caused by **Moon (chiefly) + Sun** gravity; **spring tides** (highest, new/full moon — Sun+Moon aligned), **neap tides** (lowest, quarter moon); tidal energy potential (Gulf of Kutch/Khambhat).
**Coral reefs**: warm, shallow, clean tropical seas (**Great Barrier Reef**); **coral bleaching** from warming; **Lakshadweep, Gulf of Mannar, A&N** in India.
Ocean relief order: shelf→slope→abyssal plain→trench (Mariana deepest); salinity ~35 ppt.
Spring tides (new/full moon, highest) vs Neap tides (quarter moon).

blocks.text: Water-related hazards — **floods, tsunamis, droughts and storm surges** — cause major disasters, while **marine and continental resources** (fisheries, minerals, energy, water) are vital to the economy — both especially relevant to coastal Andhra.

rows: Seismic sea-wave (earthquake/undersea landslide); **2004 Indian Ocean tsunami** hit the AP/TN coast.
Monsoon floods; **cyclonic storm surges** on the AP-Odisha coast.
**Fisheries, offshore oil/gas (KG basin), placer minerals (monazite beach sands), salt, tidal energy**.
**Freshwater, soils, forests, minerals, groundwater** on land.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: hydro disasters & marine resources

items: **Tsunami**: seismic sea-wave from undersea earthquakes/landslides (not tides); India's **2004 Indian Ocean tsunami**; **INCOIS (Hyderabad)** runs the tsunami early-warning system.
**Floods & droughts**: monsoon-dependent; delta & coastal flooding; **CWC** monitors floods; drought types (meteorological/hydrological/agricultural).

**Marine resources**: fisheries (EEZ = 200 nautical miles; India's **Blue Revolution/PMMSY**), offshore **oil & gas (Mumbai High, KG Basin)**, **polymetallic nodules** (India has a licensed CCZ site in the Indian Ocean — **Deep Ocean Mission**), tidal/wave energy, salt.
**Continental resources**: minerals, forests, soil, water; the **Exclusive Economic Zone** and **UNCLOS** framework govern ocean rights.
Tsunami (2004) & cyclonic storm surge = major AP coastal hazards; KG basin = offshore gas.
Beach-sand placer minerals (monazite) and fisheries are key marine resources.
